Case L42: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 251x251x265 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete.

**Summary — Case L42 (lipomatous soft-tissue tumor, T1 MRI):**

- **Finding:** a very large, encapsulated, fat-signal (bright on T1) multilobulated mass in the extremity, displacing the surrounding dark musculature, spanning axial slices 42–231, coronal 62–180 and sagittal 51–130 (≈19 × 12 × 8 cm; 717 mL).
- **Method:** located the lesion on axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets, seeded it with three positive points on the slice where it is largest (axial 120), then verified the outline against the lesion boundary on many additional slices in all three planes (proximal pole, mid-levels, distal tail, and medial/lateral edges).
- **Corrections:** ran one model refinement (+4 mL / −10 mL, essentially stable), reviewed all automatic intensity candidates — C1–C3 were the surrounding normal subcutaneous fat and C4/C5 tiny intermuscular fat pockets, so none were accepted.
- **Result:** single connected component, mask follows the tumour capsule throughout, including its heterogeneous periphery and the tapering distal tail.

Final confidence: **medium** (boundary well aligned, mild residual uncertainty at the superior pole and the small medial lobulations).
